context: This scenario tests whether the evaluatee correctly uses the second parameter of buildMakeReadOnly to configure class-level exclusions. The evaluatee must pass the skip list to the factory (not implement the check themselves) and verify that the package's class-name matching causes skipped instances to bypass tracking. Criteria focus on correct factory parameter usage.

checklist.name: Pass skip list to factory
checklist.description: The array of class name strings is passed as the second argument to buildMakeReadOnly, not implemented as a wrapper around the returned function.

checklist.name: Skipped class not tracked
checklist.description: When the tracking function is called on an instance of a class whose name is in the skip list, the logger is not called even after mutations to that instance's properties.

checklist.name: Non-skipped class tracked
checklist.description: Objects whose constructor name is not in the skip list are still tracked normally and trigger the logger on mutation.

checklist.name: Constructor name matching
checklist.description: The exclusion is based on constructor.name matching (the package's mechanism), not on instanceof checks or manual type guards.
